rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even people who might perform small good deeds for show are so dominated by miserliness that they cannot feign generosity even with something trivial.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من كان بهذه الصفة ربما فعل قليل الخير دون جليله رياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘withhold’ is omitted to make its scope universal: they deny everyone, whatever that person's rank or place in their hearts.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول الأول تعميماً حتى يشمل كل أحد وإن جل وعظمت منزلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿūn covers rights due on wealth and small useful things, such as lending an ordinary household utensil that people commonly share.
rows.anchor: حقوق الأموال والشيء اليسير من المنافع ، مثل إعارة التافه من متاع البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny needy people the rights God has made due in their property.
rows.anchor: ويمنعون أهل الحاجة ما أوجب الله لهم في أموالهم من الحقوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term should be read as withholding what must be given, including surplus pasture, water, zakat, and similar obligations, so the act warrants woe.
rows.anchor: ينبغي حمل ذلك على منع ما يجب بذله ، مثل فضل الكلأ والماء والزكاة ونحوه

rows.speaker: علي وابن عمر والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda interpret al-maʿūn as zakat.
rows.anchor: وعلى الزكاة حمله علي وابن عمر -رضي الله عنهما- والحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: The scholars derive al-maʿūn from al-maʿn, which denotes something slight or small.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء : هو مأخوذ من المعن ، وهو في اللغة الشيء اليسير

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpreters identify al-maʿūn as water.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فسره بعضهم بالماء ، وبعضهم بما يعار من المتاع

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret al-maʿūn as borrowed household items such as a pot, axe, or bucket.
rows.anchor: بما يعار من المتاع ، نحو القدر والفأس والدلو

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret it as zakat because zakat takes only a very small portion of one's property.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم بالزكاة ؛ لأنه لا يؤخذ من المال على وجه الزكاة إلا شيء يسير جداً

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reported definition makes al-maʿūn every gift or benefit.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو كل عطية أو منفعة

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub analyzes maʿūn as the pattern fāʿūl from maʿn, meaning customary kindness.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب : هو فاعول من المعن ، والمعن : المعروف

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says al-maʿūn meant gifts and benefits in pre-Islamic usage, and zakat in Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : الماعون في الجاهلية العطاء والمنفعة ، وفي الإسلام الزكاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines al-maʿūn as a loaned item; al-Harawī's report is cited by ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq al-Ishbīlī.
rows.anchor: وقال الهروي : قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هو العارية

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr says the basic meaning of al-maʿūn is the benefit of anything.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير : وأصل الماعون من كل شيء منفعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their contempt for a chief support of religion while magnifying the smallest worldly matters shows that they have reached the extreme of denial.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك على أنهم بلغوا نهاية التكذيب باستهانتهم بأعظم دعائم الدين ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final fault is also the sūra's first fault: denial leads to withholding; one who withholds trivial things is apt to be denied al-Kawthar at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهذا الآخر كما ترى هو الأول ؛ لأن الذي جر إليه هو التكذيب ، ومن منع هذه الأشياء التافهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra's closing returns to its opening and parallels al-Anfāl, whose corresponding beginning and end make it an explanatory counterpart worth considering alongside this sūra.
rows.anchor: وكما التقى آخرها بأولها التقت السورة كلها مع مناظرتها في العدد من أول القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra condemns low character rooted in denying recompense, neglecting people's rights and obedience to God, following defects, despising the weak, and ostentatious worship; it urges their noble opposites.
rows.anchor: حاصل هذه السورة الإبعاد عن سفساف الأخلاق ورديها ودنيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfāl 8:4 describes true believers as establishing prayer and spending from their provision, complementing the sūra's portrait of failed worship and withholding.
rows.anchor: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون أولئك هم المؤمنون حقاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfāl 8:32 quotes disbelievers challenging God to send down the truth, paralleling the sūra's denial of recompense and revelation.
rows.anchor: وإذ قالوا اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfāl 8:35 calls the unbelievers' prayer at the House whistling and clapping, matching the sūra's exposure of hollow, showy prayer.
rows.anchor: وما كان صلاتهم عند البيت إلا مكاء وتصدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfāl 8:36 says the disbelievers will be gathered to Hell, matching the warning of woe here.
rows.anchor: والذين كفروا إلى جهنم يحشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfāl 8:41 assigns shares of the spoils to God, the Messenger, kin, orphans, the needy, and travelers, addressing the sūra's refusal of due rights.
rows.anchor: فإن لله خمسه وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfāl 8:47 describes people leaving their homes boastfully to show off, paralleling this sūra's condemnation of ostentation.
rows.anchor: الذين خرجوا من ديارهم بطراً ورياء الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra has twenty-five words; reckoned from the start of the Prophetic mission, this corresponds to year twelve after the Hijra, late in Abū Bakr's caliphate.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن عدة كلماتها خمس وعشرون كلمة ، فإذا اعتبرتها من أول سني النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By then Abū Bakr had eliminated the Muslims who apostatized or withheld zakat after the Prophet's death, exposing that their earlier prayer and almsgiving had been for show.
rows.anchor: وفيها لم يبق على يده أحد من المصلين الذين ارتدوا عن الإسلام بعد وفاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو منعوا الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Bakr's forces completed the campaigns against Banū Ḥanīfa at Yamāma, the people of al-Nujayr in Kinda, and al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī at Ṣanʿāʾ within that year.
rows.anchor: بالفراغ من بني حنيفة باليمامة وأطراف بلاد اليمن من أهل النجير ببلاد كندة ، والأسود العنسي من صنعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Year sixteen, corresponding to the twenty-five words plus the basmala, saw Arab polytheists and Christians and Zoroastrians around Iraq, Syria, and Bahrain leave the peninsula; most became Muslim and the rest went to Roman lands.
rows.anchor: حتى زالوا من جميع جزيرة العرب ، وهم مشركو العرب ومتنصروهم ومتمجسوهم الذين كانوا بنواحي العراق والشام والبحرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eventual woe also reaches ostentatious worshippers: they were called to prayer by their Prophet, turned away, and others followed their example.
rows.anchor: فحل الويل بالمرائين من أهل الصلاة ، فإنهم الذين أتى إليهم نبيهم صلى الله عليه وسلم بالصلاة فأعرضوا عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no need to extract a numerical allusion from the pronouns or letter counts: the religion's public triumph leaves nothing concealed or obstructed that needs such a signal.
rows.anchor: ولم يصح في هذه السورة اعتبار الضمائر ؛ لأن الدين في هذا الحد كان قد ظهر على كل ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After al-Naṣr promised victory and the community's growth after weakness and ended by naming God the Accepter of repentance, this sūra answers whether Abū Lahab would persist or be humbled.
rows.anchor: قدم سبحانه وتعالى في سورة النصر القطع بتحقيق النصر لأهل هذا الدين بعد ما كانوا فيه من الذلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Lahab was the Prophet's close relative and a notorious, intensely hostile tormentor of him and his leadership.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو لهب - من شدة العناد لهذا الدين والأذى لإمامة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra's placement after victory recalls the early persecution and proves that the disbelievers' numbers, arms, alliances, and pacts could not defeat God's promise in 3:12.
rows.anchor: مذكراً له صلى الله عليه وسلم بما كان في أول الأمر من جبروتهم وأذاهم وقوتهم بالعَدد والعُدد ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing the Prophet's nearest enemy signals that kin and stranger are equally subject to God's judgment; kinship did not help Abū Lahab.
rows.anchor: فذكر تعالى أعداهم له وأقربهم إليه في النسب ، إشارة إلى أنه لا فرق في تكذيبه لهم بين القريب والبعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense presents the ruin as already decreed, complete, inevitable, and inescapable.
rows.anchor: فقال تعالى معبراً بالماضي دلالة على أن الأمر قد قضى بذلك وفرغ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbat conveys the greatest severance and definitive loss, ending in destruction, since only salvation in the afterlife is true salvation.
rows.anchor: أي حصل القطع الأعظم ، والحتم الأكمل ، فإنها خابت وخسرت غاية الخسارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike sister sūras introduced by qul, this sūra speaks directly in God's voice: the form is more decorous toward kin, stronger in God's vindication of the Prophet, and more immediately alarming.
rows.anchor: أكثر أدباً وأدخل في باب العذر وأولى في مراعاة ذوي الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because hands are the seat of human capacity, naming both signifies that all Abū Lahab's power failed; the dual can also stand for the whole person.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت اليد محل قدرة الإنسان ، فإذا اختلت اختل أمره ، فكيف إذا حصل الخلل في يديه جميعاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kunya, though often honorific, fits Abū Lahab's condition and makes clear that he could neither give nor withhold, help nor harm.
rows.anchor: فلا قدرة له على إعطاء ولا منع ، ولا على جلب ولا دفع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet taught that God judges hearts and deeds, not outward appearance or wealth; Abū Lahab's handsome appearance could not rescue his evil conduct.
rows.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم ولا أموالكم ، ولكن ينظر إلى قلوبكم وأعمالكم "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His kunya was given for his bright face and glowing cheeks, and its fame made it the clearest designation.
rows.anchor: لأنه إنما كني بهذا لإشراق وجهه وتوقد وجنتيه ، ولأنها أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the kunya is more fitting than his personal name ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, which is repugnant because servitude should not be attributed to an unworthy object.
rows.anchor: لأن اسمه عبد العزى ، وهو قبيح موجب للعدول عنه غيرة على العبودية أن تضاف إلى غير مستحقها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads this sūra with what precedes as a declaration that Muḥammad has completed the trust of messengership and his life is near its end, signaled by people entering Islam in crowds.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : هذه السورة وإن نزلت على سبب خاص ، وفي قصة معلومة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says woe awaits anyone who opposes the Prophet and departs from following him, even his closest relative.
rows.anchor: والويل لمن عاندك وعدل عن متابعتك ، وإن كان أقرب الناس إليك

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says al-Kāfirūn separated allies from enemies and made clear the status of those who follow the Prophet and those who oppose him.
rows.anchor: فقد فصلت سورة { قل يا أيها الكافرون } بين أوليائك وأعدائك ،

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reports that the Prophet called al-Kāfirūn the sūra that clears its reader of hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: ولهذا سماها عليه الصلاة والسلام المبرئة من النفاق

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says only faith protects anyone from Hell; kinship alone offers no benefit, as shown by Abū Lahab despite being the Prophet's uncle.
rows.anchor: وليعلم كفار قريش وغيرهم أنه لا اعتصام لأحد من النار إلا بالإيمان ، وأن القرابات غير نافعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause makes explicit that the ruin concerns Abū Lahab himself in his entirety, not merely literal loss of his hands.
rows.anchor: وكان الإنسان لا يزول جميع منفعته بفوات يديه ، وإن كان قد يعبر بهما عن النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent construction is a curse or prayer in the first clause followed by a factual report in the second.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الأول دعاء ، والثاني خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clarification confirms the hand-expression as a figure for utter destruction, leaving no life or recovery afterward.
rows.anchor: فحقق بهذا ما أريد من الإسناد إلى اليدين من الكناية عن الهلاك الذي لا بقاء بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being related to a righteous person does not avail without following that person's deeds; Abū Lahab was the Prophet's uncle.
rows.anchor: وعرف بهذا أن الانتماء إلى الصالحين لا يغني إلا إن وقع الاقتداء بهم في أفعالهم ؛ لأنه عم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The roots tabb and batt center on severance that commonly leads to ruin: severing oneself from the ultimate Cause for lesser means brings loss, and exhausting all means can still frustrate one's aims.
rows.anchor: تدور على القطع المؤدي في أغلب أحواله إلى الهلاك ؛ لأن من انقطع إلى الأسباب معرضاً عن مسببها

rows.speaker: ابن مكتوم
rows.claim: Ibn Maktūm's lexicon defines tabb and tibāb as loss, and tabban lahu as a curse; tabban tabīban intensifies it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مكتوم في الجمع بين المحكم والعباب : التب والتباب : الخسار ،

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz parses tabban lahu as a verbal noun meaning ‘loss to him,’ accusative like suqyan lahu.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو عبد الله القزاز : كأنك قلت : خسراناً له ، وهو المصدر ، نصب نصب سقياً له

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd distinguishes tabb as a verbal noun from tibāb as a noun; tabab, tibāb, and tabīb mean ruin, while tatbīb means deficiency and loss.
rows.anchor: قال ابن دريد : وكأن التب المصدر ، والتباب الاسم ، والتبب والتباب والتبيب : الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other lexical senses extend the root to an old man or woman, a weak person, and a donkey or camel with a damaged back, all suggesting decline toward severance or death.
rows.anchor: والتابّ : الكبير من الرجال ، والأنثى تابة .

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz explains tabba as an old, failing woman, a sense linked to age's nearness to severance and death.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز : إذا سألت الرجل عن المرأة ، قلت : أشابة هي أم تابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabba can mean ‘cut’ like batt; falling into tabūb or being in tabba describes a dire condition; tibbi is a low-grade Bahrain date eaten by common people.
rows.anchor: وتب : قطع مثل بت ، أي بتقديم الموحدة ، ووقعوا في تبوب منكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Derived forms mean weakening someone's strength, destroying them, or growing old, continuing the root's sense of decline and ruin.
rows.anchor: وأتب الله قوته : أضعفها . وتببوهم تتبيباً : أهلكوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tubūb can denote the chest or heart enclosed by the ribs; this may be read positively or negatively because a sound or corrupt heart affects the whole body.
rows.anchor: والتبوب -يعني بالضم- : ما انطوت عليه الأضلاع كالصدر والقلب

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz says istatabba means that a matter became prepared and settled; he also notes that a proposed analogy does not hold in comparable expressions.
rows.anchor: واستتب الأمر : تهيأ واستوى . وقال القزاز : ويقال : هذه العلة لا تستتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author associates the sīn in istatabba with completion, interpreting it as bringing the matter fully to success and clarity.
rows.anchor: كأنه من باب الإزالة إذ إن السين لما جامعت حرفي السببين آذنت بالنجاح والفوز والفلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reversed root batt makes explicit the stronger, outward severance that depends on a complete inward cause.
rows.anchor: والذي يحقق معاني التب ، ويظهر أنه يؤول إلى القطع مقلوبه ، وهو البت - بتقديم الموحدة- التي هي السبب الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Batt and abatta mean to cut something completely; alignment across basic, derived, intransitive, and transitive forms suggests the cutting is already maximal.
rows.anchor: يقال : بت الشيء يبته بتاً ، وأبته : قطعه قطعاً مستأصلاً

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says qaʿada al-battata is an emphatic verbal noun construction, used only with the definite article.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه : وقالوا : قعد البتة ، مصدر مؤكد ، ولا يستعمل إلا بالألف واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root appears in definitive truth, irrevocable triple divorce, and al-battata (‘never’), figuratively severing doubt, return, or an intended act.
rows.anchor: وصدقه بتة : بتلة باينة من صاحبها ، وطلقها ثلاثاً بتة وإبتاتاً ، أي قطعاً لا عود فيه

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz distinguishes yubittu from abatta and yabittu from batta; batt describes incoherent drunken speech, and a batt drunkard is cut off from work.
rows.anchor: قال القزاز : يبت من أبت ، ويبَت من بَتَّ ، وسكران باتّ : منقطع عن العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abatta can mean to carry through an oath, while battat can mean that something became established or due; both derive from severance.
rows.anchor: وأبت يمينه : أمضاها ، أي قطعها عن الحنث ، وبتت هي : وجبت وحلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith calls the person who exhausts his mount until its back fails al-munbat, leaving him stranded; al-Qazzāz gives the same explanation.
rows.anchor: والمنبت في الحديث : الذي أتعب دابته حتى عطب ظهره ، فبقي منقطعاً به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also describes fixing or imposing testimony and judgment; a bat is an emaciated person too weak to stand, as though his strength were cut off.
rows.anchor: وبت عليه الشهادة وأبتها : قطع عليه بها ، وألزمه إياها ، وبت عليه القضاء وأبته ، قطعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith's phrase ‘no fast for one who did not yubit fasting at night’ means resolving and obligating the fast before dawn; yubit from batta is another eloquent form with the same meaning, and a version uses yabit from bayāt.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث  "  لا صيام لمن لم يبت الصيام من الليل "  . فمعناه : يوجبه

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines ahmaq batt as extreme foolishness; al-Azharī instead says the word is tabb, with bāʾ delayed.
rows.anchor: وأحمق بات : شديد الحمق ، كذا قاله الليث ، وقال الأزهري : هو تاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-batt is a coarse, loose, square green cloak, said to be made of camel hair and wool; its plural is butūt.
rows.anchor: والبت : كساء غليظ مهلهل مربع أخضر ، وقيل : هو من وبر وصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-battāt means household belongings or travel provisions, either because they cut off need or because they remove deprivation by supplying and helping the owner.
rows.anchor: والبتات- أي بالتخفيف- : متاع البيت والزاد ، كأن ذلك يقطع صاحبه عن الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author proposes that each root family has a dominant sense and forms that remove or reverse it; assistance and provision exemplify such removal.
rows.anchor: لأن الاستقراء حاصل بأن كل مادة لها معنى غالب تدور عليه ، وفيها شيء لإزالة ذلك المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being ʿalā battat amr means nearing completion, when the matter is about to end.
rows.anchor: وفلان على بتات أمر إذا أشرف على فراغه ، فإنه ينقطع حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grinding with the mill turning leftward marks fully resolved purpose because it gives the grinder greater strength and control.
rows.anchor: وتقول : طحنت بالرحى بتاً إذا ابتدأت الإدارة عن يسارك ، كأنه دال على القطع بتمام العزيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inbatt can mean a man's semen was depleted; a single-strand cord is called batt because it is easily cut, and inbatta ʿan someone means he withdrew and severed contact.
rows.anchor: وانبت الرجل : انقطع ماء ظهره ، ويقال : هذا حبل بتّ : إذا كان طاقاً واحداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the emphatic announcement of ruin, the verse answers disbelievers who presumed wealth, children, and strength could secure them, declaring worldly circumstances useless.
rows.anchor: ولما أوقع سبحانه الإخبار بهلاكه على هذا الوجه المؤكد لما كان لصاحب القصة وغيره من الكفار من التكذيب بلسان حاله وقاله لما له من المال والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction may be read as an informative statement or as a rebuking rhetorical question.
rows.anchor: فقال مخبراً ، أو مستفهماً منكراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aghnā means to suffice, benefit, or meet a need; ‘against him’ means against Abū Lahab, the wretched outcast banished from mercy and punished.
rows.anchor: أي أجزى وناب وسد { عنه } أي عن أبي لهب الشقي الطريد المبعود عن الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His abundant wealth was the kind people customarily expect to save them from destruction, yet it did not.
rows.anchor: { ماله } أي الكثير الذي جرت العادة بأنه ينجي من الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What one earns is broader than money: property can produce greater benefits such as status, and a person may prosper through achievements gained by effort without wealth.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الكسب أعم من المال ، وكان المال قد يكسب منافع هي أعظم منه من الجاه وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing benefits except what God commands; ‘what he earned’ includes children, companions, and clan prestige, which Abū Lahab used to harm and deny the Prophet publicly and discourage belief despite formerly calling him truthful and trustworthy.
rows.anchor: مبيناً أنه لا ينفع إلا ما أمر الله به

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed that God set one of His dogs against ʿUtba, Abū Lahab's son, who had severely mistreated him.
rows.anchor: حتى قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : " اللهم سلط عليه كلباً من كلابك "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Lahab feared the Prophet's prayer and sent his son toward Syria with companions instructed to protect him, but a lion found and killed him despite their precautions.
rows.anchor: فكان أبو لهب يعرف أن هذه الدعوة لا بد أن تدركه ، فلما حان الأمر ، وكان قد آن ما أراد صاحب العز الشامخ

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ recounts that at Badr Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith described the defeat and white riders on piebald horses in the sky who overwhelmed the Meccans; Rāfiʿ recognized them as angels.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رافع غلام العباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنه- وكان جالساً في حجرة في المسجد يبري نبلاً

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان بن الحارث
rows.claim: Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith told Abū Lahab that at Badr the Muslims routed them, taking prisoners as they wished, and that white riders in the sky could not be resisted.
rows.anchor: كان منهم ابن أخيه أبو سفيان بن الحارث فقال : هلم يا ابن أخي ، فعندك الخبر

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abū Lahab struck the weak Abū Rāfiʿ, knocked him down, and beat him after he called the unseen fighters angels; Umm al-Faḍl split Abū Lahab's head with a tent pole and rebuked him for attacking her servant while his master was away.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رافع غلام العباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنه- وكان جالساً في حجرة في المسجد يبري نبلاً

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ says Abū Lahab left humiliated and died six or seven nights later when God struck him with al-ʿadasa.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رافع غلام العباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz describes al-ʿadasa as a usually fatal, plague-like pustule resembling a lentil; in pre-Islamic times it was thought contagious and few survived it.
rows.anchor: والعدسة بثرة تشبه العدسة تخرج في مواضع من الجسد من جنس الطاعون تقتل غالباً ، قال القزاز : كانت تعدي في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disease is called ʿadasa; one says ʿadasa al-rajul or huwa maʿdūs, as one says ṭuʿina or maṭʿūn for being struck by plague.
rows.anchor: تقول : عدس الرجل فهو معدوس ، كما تقول : طعن فهو مطعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Arabs feared al-ʿadasa, Abū Lahab's body was left unburied for three days until it stank, then hired Sudanese men buried it; another account says they pushed it into a distant pit with poles and threw stones and earth from afar.
rows.anchor: ولأجل تشاؤم العرب بها ترك أبو لهب من غير دفن ثلاثاً ، حتى أنتن ، ثم استأجروا بعض السودان حتى دفنوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distant stoning of the grave became a custom, and Abū Lahab is still stoned; this was an early sign of the verses' miraculous truth, since nothing he thought would save him prevented his disgrace among Arabs.
rows.anchor: فكان ذلك سنة في رجمه ، فهو يرجم إلى الآن ، وذلك من أول إعجاز هذه الآيات
